title: Visual Similarity in Adult Word Extension and Artificial Word Learning
abstract: arXiv:2611.14116v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When two objects share a name, how much does their visual similarity explain, and what do the teaching examples add? First, we reanalyzed trial-level data from a large adult word-extension study (Lewis & Frank, 2018), computing each test image's distance to the examples shown in the space of a frozen self-supervised visual encoder (DINOv2). Distance was associated with extension (log odds -3.23 per standard deviation; 520 people), and an exploratory post hoc analysis suggested that this association persisted within the taught domain after controlling for taxonomic level and teaching condition. Example composition also mattered: after three examples, adults extended a word to 1.1% of superordinate items when the examples were subordinate and to 77.5% when they were superordinate. translated_title: 成人词汇扩展与人造词汇学习中的视觉相似性
translated_abstract: 当两个物体共享同一个名称时，它们的视觉相似性能在多大程度上解释这一现象，教学示例又能带来什么额外作用？首先，我们重新分析了一项大型成人词汇扩展研究的试验级数据（Lewis & Frank, 2018），在冻结的自监督视觉编码器（DINOv2）的空间中计算每个测试图像与所展示示例之间的距离。距离与词汇扩展显著相关（每标准差对数几率为-3.23；共520名参与者），一项探索性事后分析表明，在控制了分类层级和教学条件后，这种关联在已教授的领域内依然存在。示例的组成同样重要：在学习三个示例后，当示例为下位类别时，成人仅将词汇扩展到上位类别项目的1.1%，而当示例为上位类别时，这一比例达到77.5%。其次，在使用同一编码器的人工学习者实验中，当一个词连接两个类别时，类别之间距离越远，学习准确度越低（84.7%……
tldr: 本研究通过重新分析大规模成人词汇扩展数据并进行人工词汇学习实验，利用冻结的自监督视觉编码器（DINOv2）量化物体间的视觉相似性，发现视觉距离显著影响词汇的扩展范围，且教学示例的类别层级高低决定了学习者在多大程度上将词汇泛化到更广泛或更具体的类别。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates, via reanalysis of a large adult word-extension dataset and an artificial word-learning experiment, that visual similarity measured by frozen self-supervised encoder (DINOv2) distances predicts word extension, and that the taxonomic level of teaching examples determines how broadly learners generalize a word to other categories.
